issues.legal_issue: A wakf board cannot maintain a suit for declaration and possession of property omitted from the published wakf list unless it first follows the statutory procedure for determining that the property is wakf property.
material_facts: The wakf board brought suits seeking possession of properties said to have been dedicated for charitable and religious purposes.
The courts found that the suit properties were not included in the published list of wakf properties.
The board had not used the statutory process for investigating and determining whether the omitted properties were wakf properties.
The board relied on the principle that a permanent dedication remains wakf property, but the decision below rested on the board’s failure to follow the statutory procedure.
issues.conclusion: The board could not maintain the suits for declaration and possession without first complying with the statutory procedure; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 5 of the Wakf Act, 1954, wakf properties are surveyed and published in a list. Section 6 provides for a civil suit by a person aggrieved by the list within the prescribed period, not at the instance of the Wakf Board. For a property omitted from the list, Section 27 empowers the Board to collect information, make an inquiry, and decide whether the property is wakf property; that decision is final unless revoked or modified by a civil court. The Board must follow the applicable statutory procedure before bringing a suit for declaration and possession. Sayyed Ali was cited for the continuing character of wakf property, but the Court did not treat that principle as dispensing with the procedural requirements.

predicates.wakf_board_filed_possession_suit: A wakf board brought a suit seeking possession of property claimed to be wakf property.
predicates.property_omitted_from_published_list: The property at issue was not included in the published list of wakf properties.
predicates.board_did_not_complete_property_determin: The board did not complete the statutory inquiry and determination process for the omitted property before suing.

issues.definition: When a wakf board sues for possession of property omitted from the published list without first completing the property-determination process, it cannot maintain the declaration and possession suit.
